page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V platform. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor capable of clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores via symmetric multithreading. Memory allocation is substantial, offering 32.0 GB of system RAM, which establishes an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per core). The underlying processor includes a large 260 MB L3 cache and supports specialized instruction sets, including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8. Storage capacity includes a local 236 GB NVMe SSD intended for temporary storage and high-speed scratch space, with no discrete GPU accelerators attached.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread execution paired with moderate overall parallel capacity. The server achieves a strong single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.35 GB/sec and average tier results across single-core Geekbench (1643.0) and PassMark CPU metrics (7381.13 total CPU score, 5612.97 extended instructions). Memory bandwidth measures 36.24 GB/sec for large block reads and 25.93 GB/sec for writes. However, overall multi-core throughput falls into the lower quartile, reflecting the two-physical-core ceiling; multi-core Geekbench scores 3707.0, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression runs at 26.0 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput delivers 5.66 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput reaches 7.57 GB/sec, and lightweight LLM inference handles small 135M parameter models at 436.99 prompt tokens per second.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the instance trades high multi-core compute density for memory capacity and high clock speeds. This makes the E4ds_v6 resource-efficient for environments where licensing or architecture favors smaller vCPU counts with elevated memory thresholds, avoiding the expense of higher core-count instances. Primary operational workloads include relational database management systems, intermediate caching layers, data wrangling pipelines, and memory-bound backend applications that benefit from local NVMe temporary storage.
